answer_1.quote: We conduct experiments with a number of representative open-source and closed-source LLMs ... to evaluate LLMs on HaluEval 2.0 and apply our detection approach to measure their tendency to produce hallucinations.

answer_2.quote: We design two metrics from different levels to measure the degree of LLMs generating hallucinations in their responses. The micro hallucination rate (MiHR) ... The macro hallucination rate (MaHR) ... We also use BERTScore to select difficult questions.

answer_3.quote: We instruct a LLM (i.e., GPT‑4) to extract factual statements ... Second, we use the LLM itself to judge the trustfulness of statements since the LLM has encoded rich world knowledge.

answer_4.quote: We invite human labelers to annotate the factuality of a subset from HaluEval 2.0 ... each sample is labeled by two labelers and examined by one checker.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators label the hallucination type of each statement (e.g., entity-error, relation-error, incompleteness, outdatedness, overclaim, unverifiability).
